messages:
maya (eng-runtime): heads up — ran the scheduled warmers this morning after the kernel selector change. quick summary below, want eyes on keying + rollout plan
ankur (infra): nice. did you use the new normalizing key function?
sara (perf): short version: yes, and results are... interesting. overall cache hit-rate jumped, but we saw a regression on cold-start 95p for long prompts
maya (eng-runtime): metrics: baseline hit-rate before change ~12% (prefix normalization was inconsistent), after change -> 46% average over 2h window. warmed pods served ~62% of requests from KV.
liam (prod-eng): that 46% is huge. what's the cost delta from running warmers?
maya (eng-runtime): cost ~+4% CPU on warmers job, GPU time negligible (we limited synthetic traffic to small batch sizes). price delta looks acceptable compared to latency wins.
sara (perf): specifics: 95th latency on small prompt paths dropped by ~120ms on warmed routes. but for long sequence requests (seq>1024) we saw a small regression: 95p +90ms for first token when warmer was active. suspect kernel selection fallback interaction.
ankur (infra): logs show extra kernel-switch overhead when a pod receives warm cache entries then immediately gets a long sequence that forces different kernel. possibly due to late kernel probe during runtime init.
maya (eng-runtime): repro snippet from one pod: 
```
[2026-02-15T07:12:33Z] chosen_kernel=quant-opt-v2
[2026-02-15T07:12:33Z] kv_prefill=true
[2026-02-15T07:12:33Z] incoming.seq_len=2048, kernel_probe=fp16-attn
[2026-02-15T07:12:34Z] kernel_reload=+85ms
```
ankur (infra): that matches. warmers primed KV keys for short prefixes which hit quant-opt-v2. when a long request forces fallback, we pay kernel_reload.
sara (perf): hypothesis: warmer should include representative longer sample inputs (not just the short, high-frequency prefixes). also consider delaying kernel probe by checking likely-seq distribution before switching.
liam (prod-eng): operational question: should scheduled warmers target every deploy or only when autoscaler scales? current runbook: nightly cron, plus manual predeploy hook for major rollouts.
maya (eng-runtime): ran three experiments: 1) deploy-time warmers (post-deploy job that hits new pods), 2) autoscale-triggered warmers (hook into HPA scale-up events), 3) scheduled cron (every 2h).
maya (eng-runtime): results: deploy-time warmers gave fast warm cache hit-rates on canaries but missed traffic patterns from real users. autoscale-triggered gave best steady-state: when we scale up 3+ pods, warmers bring hit-rate to 40-55% in ~45s. scheduled cron maintained baseline but had slow recovery after spikes.
ankur (infra): autoscale hook implementation note: we used k8s event listener that POSTs a small synthetic batch to /internal/warm?model=<model>&seed=hash. sample curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://svc.internal/warm?model=gptx-10b -d '{"prompts": ["Hello world"], "replicas":2}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARMER_TOKEN'
```
sara (perf): warm payloads used for autoscale were 3 variants: short prefix (avg user), long prefix (heavy tail), and a random 2x repeat to exercise KV merging. that fixed the kernel-switch regression in the next run.
liam (prod-eng): any impact on client-visible cache keying? did we normalize user-provided prompt metadata?
maya (eng-runtime): yes we changed keying to canonicalize whitespace, strip session-only metadata and collapse variable placeholders. the key is now sha1(prefix_normalized || model || quant_profile). that reduced duplicate keys and raised hit-rate.
ankur (infra): TTLs: we tested TTL 15m, 1h, and sticky (no TTL with LRU eviction). 15m gave best balance for bursty traffic; 1h increased hit-rate but caused stale kv combos after model patching. sticky led to stale regressions during canary rollouts.
sara (perf): recommended defaults: TTL=20m, attach warmers to deploy event with a short forced eviction window right after model rollback to avoid stale prefix mismatches.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary v2.14 -> stable v2.14 at 2026-02-15T08:00:12Z :rocket:
maya (eng-runtime): note: we observed a small regression when we flipped compilation kernels in the selector (night change). correlation: kernel binary compatibility + sticky kv entries -> mismatched kv encoding. fixed by tagging kv entries with kernel_version in the key (added as metadata before sha1).
liam (prod-eng): good catch. that suggests every kernel selector or quant profile change must trigger kv eviction for affected pods. add a flag to the rollout pipeline.
ankur (infra): ops idea: when a deploy changes kernel ABI, we broadcast an event that triggers `curl https://svc.internal/warm?evict=true&tag=kernel_vX` then re-run warmers.
sara (perf): for synthetic traffic strategy: keep batch sizes at 4 and qps <= 10 per pod during warm to avoid warming cost explosion; measure tokens_generated and warm_success_count metric. goal: warm_hit_rate >= 40% within 60s of pod start.
maya (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add canary warmer step to deploy pipeline (post-canary, pre-promote) 2) hook warmers to HPA scale events 3) update keying to include kernel_version and quant_profile 4) set TTL default to 20m 5) add warm_job metrics (warm_start_ts, warm_duration_ms, warm_hit_delta).
liam (prod-eng): ok please open runbook PR and a small infra change for HPA hook. want conservative rollout: enable on one model pool for a week.
maya (eng-runtime): will do. draft runbook notes in PR and tag @ankur @sara for review. cc ops-bot for future automation. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: noted — creating scheduled task entry and HPA listener ticket #A-4921
maya (eng-runtime): thanks all, i'll attach graphs to the PR: hit-rate over time, 95/50 latency deltas, and kernel-switch logs. anyone wants raw traces ping me and i'll share a quick query.
liam (prod-eng): thanks — big win overall. small risks, plan looks solid.
sara (perf): one more: add integration test that simulates kernel-flip + warmers to catch regressions in CI.
maya (eng-runtime): added to backlog. end thread.
